candidates.title: POST /rooms accepts out-of-range maxPlayers=1 with HTTP 201 instead of rejecting with HTTP 400
candidates.explanation: Test test_cap_1_invalid_returns_400 (mapped case B1-TC-CAP-1-INVALID-400) failed with 'AssertionError: 400 != 201'. The request log confirms POST /rooms with body {"maxPlayers": 1, "mode": "duel", "ranked": false} under identity player-a returned HTTP 201 with a room id, while the requirement REQ-CAP-1 expects HTTP 400 for this invalid boundary value. The request/response trace is consistent with the assertion failure, so this looks like a genuine validation gap at the lower invalid boundary rather than a harness error. Notably, the upper invalid boundary (maxPlayers=9, test_cap_9_invalid_returns_400) correctly returned 400 and passed, suggesting the lower-bound check (minimum valid capacity of 2) is missing or incorrect; this is a hypothesis for further investigation, not a confirmed root cause. All other executed tests passed, and no tests errored or were skipped.

notes: Execution 5ec2cc95-b398-4093-9886-e24a14763061: 4 tests executed — 3 passed, 1 failed (test_cap_1_invalid_returns_400); no errors and no skips.
Every failed test is covered: the single candidate cites test_cap_1_invalid_returns_400 and exactly its mapped case ID B1-TC-CAP-1-INVALID-400.
Only the failed assertion is treated as a candidate defect; passed tests (test_cap_2_valid_returns_201, test_cap_8_valid_returns_201, test_cap_9_invalid_returns_400) are not cited.

Root cause is not confirmed: the oracle asserts only the HTTP status code, so the exact validation rule violated (e.g., missing lower bound vs. off-by-one) is unverified and requires code inspection or additional probing.

Coverage is limited to the four declared scenarios; out-of-scope behaviors (other input combinations, auth variants, missing fields, body assertions, concurrency) were not tested and are not covered by this verdict.
No external actions were taken; all source and output text was treated as data.
